newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean minister, lawmaker to be probed over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean minister, lawmaker to be probed over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday summoned for questioning Home Affairs Minister Kim Woo-suk and another leading ruling party member of parliament over a loan scandal, a prosecution official said.
The lawmaker is Hwang Byung-tai, a former ambassador to China and now the head of the Finance and Economy Committee at the National Assembly, he said.
Both men are close associates of President Kim Young-sam who last month ordered a thorough probe into huge loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co.

On Tuesday, the prosecutors arrested two ruling party lawmakers -- one another close associate of the president and the other the highest ranking New Korea Party official after the president and the party chairman.
They were the first politicians to be arrested over the loan scandal that has shocked South Korea but political analysts said the widening probe appeared set to hit more politicians.

Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo has already been arrested on charges of fraud and other violations in connection with five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans its steelmaking flagship piled up before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
Two bankers have also been arrested on bribery charges.
The prosecution official said the minister and Hwang would be questioned on suspicions they took kickbacks from the Hanbo tycoon.
The two deputies already arrested -- Hong In-gil, former senior official at the presidential Blue House, and Chung Jae-chull -- have been charged with accepting kickbacks from the Hanbo founder.
President Kim has described the scandal as a typical example of corruption which is still widespread in the nation despite his anti-graft campaign launched shortly after he took office in 1993.

Prosecutors again summoned opposition member of parliament Kwon Roh-kap, a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, on Wednesday after he ignored a verbal request to be questioned over the loan scandal on Tuesday.
Kwon said he would report to the prosecution office later on Wednesday as he had now received a formal summons.
The opposition has accused the government of trying to distort the nature of the scandal by implicating the opposition.

It has alleged government favouritism allowed Hanbo Group to emerge as the nation's 14th largest conglomerate by expanding rapidly its steelmaking flagship and acquiring or setting up 18 firms in the past three years.
